sets.title: Find the cause and the result

questions.prompt: The bank tightened verification ___ several fraudulent applications had been detected.
questions.clue: Detected fraud is the reason for tighter checks.
questions.rule: Because introduces a reason clause with a subject and verb.
questions.completed: The bank tightened verification because several fraudulent applications had been detected.

optionReasons.although: Would present fraud as a concession, not the reason.
optionReasons.unless: Introduces a condition that does not preserve this factual reason.
optionReasons.because of: Requires a noun phrase or -ing form, not this finite clause.
optionReasons.therefore: A result adverb cannot replace the reason conjunction here.
optionReasons.because: Because introduces a reason clause with a subject and verb.

questions.prompt: Several fraudulent applications were detected; ___, the bank tightened verification.
questions.clue: The first clause states the cause; the second states its consequence.
questions.rule: Therefore links a result clause; the semicolon and comma provide the structure.
questions.completed: Several fraudulent applications were detected; therefore, the bank tightened verification.

optionReasons.however: Marks contrast rather than the stated consequence.
optionReasons.nevertheless: Suggests an outcome despite the first fact, rather than because of it.
optionReasons.otherwise: States an alternative consequence if an action is not taken.
optionReasons.because: Would require a reason clause, not this result-adverb position.
optionReasons.therefore: Therefore links a result clause; the semicolon and comma provide the structure.

questions.prompt: The workshop postponed production ___ a shortage of essential materials.
questions.clue: The shortage causes the postponement.
questions.rule: Because of takes a noun phrase: a shortage of materials.
questions.completed: The workshop postponed production because of a shortage of essential materials.

optionReasons.because: Needs a subject and finite verb after it.
optionReasons.although: Needs a clause and introduces concession.
optionReasons.so that: Introduces a purpose clause, not a noun phrase giving a cause.
optionReasons.despite: Would say production was postponed in spite of the shortage, changing the intended reason.
optionReasons.because of: Because of takes a noun phrase: a shortage of materials.

questions.prompt: The auditor found an anomaly, ___ she examined the supporting invoices.

optionReasons.because of: Cannot introduce the finite clause she examined.
optionReasons.unless: Turns the examination into a condition rather than a response.
optionReasons.whereas: Contrasts two facts rather than showing this response.
optionReasons.therefore: A standalone linking adverb would need stronger punctuation here; the comma alone makes a splice.
optionReasons.so: So coordinates a consequence clause after a comma.

optionReasons.conversely: Would reverse a relationship, which is not intended.
optionReasons.nevertheless: Signals concession rather than the expected effect.
optionReasons.whereas: A subordinate conjunction does not fit this semicolon-adverb-comma construction.
optionReasons.consequently: Consequently introduces the result, not a contrast.

optionReasons.Despite: Despite takes a noun phrase; although takes a clause.

optionReasons.consequently: Also imposes an unsupported result relationship.

The firm delayed payment because its long-term assets were weak, not because it lacked liquidity.

The firm delayed payment unless it lacked liquidity and its long-term assets were weak.

Since the evidence corroborated the complaint, the bank reopened the case.

cards.hinglish: sirf iske baad; main clause invert

cards.meaning: Restricts an action until a specified point.
cards.pattern: Not until time/clause + inverted main clause
cards.trap: After did use the base verb.
cards.hinglish: tab tak nahi; fronted form mein inversion

cards.meaning: Often introduces the intended outcome; it can also express result in suitable contexts.
cards.pattern: action so that + subject + modal/finite verb
cards.trap: Do not force in order to before a complete subject-verb clause.
cards.hinglish: taaki: next clause ka subject ho sakta hai

cards.meaning: Introduces an intended action.
cards.trap: For a different subject use an appropriate for + subject + to structure, not a bare finite clause.

cards.meaning: Connects a degree of quality with its result.
cards.trap: Distinguish from such + noun phrase.

cards.meaning: Connects an emphasised noun phrase with its result.
cards.pattern: such + a/an + adjective + noun + that clause
cards.trap: Do not use such directly as a substitute for so before an adjective alone.

cards.meaning: Adds another fact or benefit.
cards.pattern: and coordinates; moreover links separated clauses
cards.trap: Do not invent a causal link between two facts merely being added.

cards.meaning: Adds and emphasises two parallel points.
cards.pattern: Not only did + subject + base verb, but ... also ...
cards.trap: Fronted not only requires inversion; maintain parallel structures.
cards.hinglish: dono points; pehle clause mein inversion

cards.meaning: Chooses or substitutes one alternative instead of another.
cards.trap: As well as would add Y instead of excluding it.

cards.meaning: Introduces alternatives or an indirect yes/no question.
cards.pattern: whether X or Y; whether or not
cards.trap: Do not change an either-way obligation into an only-if requirement.

cards.meaning: Excludes a stated subset or circumstance.
cards.trap: An exception to a group is not the same as a full unless-clause.

cards.meaning: Expresses an equal degree of a quality.
cards.trap: More normally pairs with than, not as.

cards.meaning: Introduces the content of a statement, belief or acknowledgement.
cards.trap: Sometimes a blank is reported content, not cause or positive/negative tone.
